title: Detention and Semester
premise: Quentin Thornbury has spent twelve years surviving Ashgrove Prep by being invisible — tracking every rigged grade, every hushed expulsion, every scholarship quietly revoked. When her best friend Marisol vanishes overnight, leaving only a janitor's keyring on Quentin's desk, Quentin discovers Marisol had been secretly compiling evidence that the school board buried a decades-old cover-up tied to a student's death. Following the keys through locked basements and sealed records rooms, Quentin must decide whether exposing the truth is worth the safety she's spent her whole life protecting. In the end she testifies before an independent investigator, the board collapses, Marisol is found alive but changed — and Quentin learns that survival without memory is just another kind of disappearance.
about_author: E. M. Villalobos is a former high school debate coach who grew up in a border town where school board minutes were read like scripture. They write stories about kids who keep receipts.

chapters.title: The Careful Girl
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. We meet her mid-semester, cataloguing anomalies in Ashgrove's grading system from the back row of the gym, invisible by design. She narrates her twelve-year strategy of never standing out. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness — competence as armor.

chapters.title: Marisol's Keys
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Marisol misses their morning coffee ritual, then doesn't show to class. At lunch Quentin finds a janitor's keyring taped under her own desk with a note: 'B-2. Don't trust Whitlock.' Emotional beat: dread blooming beneath routine.

chapters.title: Basement B-2
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, night scene. Using the keys, she enters the sub-basement and finds Marisol's hidden cache: photocopies, a 1998 newspaper clipping about a drowned student named Caleb Reyes, and a half-finished timeline. Emotional beat: vertigo — the game was always rigged, and Marisol knew.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV with flashbacks assembled from documents. The 1998 'accident' connects to then-principal Aldous Whitlock, now superintendent; three witnesses were expelled within a month. Emotional beat: cold fury hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Missing Persons
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Quentin and Detective Okafor. Police call Marisol a runaway; her mother disagrees. Quentin withholds the keys, terrified of becoming a suspect. Emotional beat: guilt of the accomplice who did nothing wrong but feels complicit.

chapters.title: The Statistician's Ledger
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She applies her statistical mind to twelve years of school data and finds a pattern: every student who questioned the Reyes story left within ninety days. Emotional beat: the price of survival made arithmetic — she was next on the list.

chapters.title: Whitlock Smiles
chapters.summary: Whitlock's POV. A polished assembly celebrating Ashgrove's centennial; he notices Quentin watching him and offers her a college recommendation she never asked for. Emotional beat: velvet menace — the predator acknowledging prey.

chapters.title: An Ally With Scratches
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Quentin and Theo, the night custodian whose father worked at Ashgrove in 1998. Theo admits some of the keys are his father's, and that Marisol came to him weeks ago. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, two people deciding trust is worth the risk.

chapters.title: Room 114
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He opens the old records room and they find sealed transcripts, including Caleb Reyes's final disciplinary hearing — falsified. Someone has recently been there: fresh tape, missing pages. Emotional beat: hope curdling into urgency — someone else knows.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, reflective chapter. Flashbacks to age six, when her family learned what happens to families who complain. Her mother's voice: 'Be careful it hurts.' Emotional beat: grief for the childhood spent crouching.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She uploads scans to an encrypted drive and contacts a local journalist, Dana Ferro, who warns her the paper was sued into silence once before. Emotional beat: first act of open rebellion — terror and exhilaration braided together.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Detective Okafor's POV. Okafor interviews Quentin, revealing off-record that Marisol's phone last pinged near the school at 11 p.m., not the bus station. Emotional beat: the law's limits — justice outside the system begins here.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Her locker is emptied, her laptop stolen, and a disciplinary file appears bearing her name — fabricated. Whitlock suspends her pending review. Emotional beat: the machine turning its gears against her precisely as predicted.

chapters.title: Underground
chapters.summary: Theo and Quentin's alternating POV. Hiding in the maintenance tunnels during school hours, they map which doors Marisol's keys open and realize one key fits nothing in the building — except the old natatorium, sealed since 1998. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: The Natatorium
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Behind a false wall they find Caleb's belongings and a maintenance log proving staff drained the pool the night he died — and a recent footprint in the dust. Someone has been back. Emotional beat: the past is not buried; it is maintained.

chapters.title: Ferro's Deadline
chapters.summary: Dana Ferro's POV. The journalist confirms the drive's contents are publishable but needs a named source; meanwhile Whitlock's lawyer files an injunction. Quentin must decide whether to go public. Emotional beat: the price of survival comes due — anonymity or truth, not both.

chapters.title: Where Marisol Went
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (revealed). She wasn't taken — she went underground deliberately after someone ransacked her cache, hiding with Theo's cousin while finishing the timeline. But her last entry names a second conspirator still employed. Emotional beat: relief laced with betrayal — the danger isn't over.

chapters.title: The Second Name
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Cross-referencing payroll and the 1998 log, she identifies Vice Principal Hargrove as the living witness-turned-accomplice. Confronting him, she records his panicked half-confession. Emotional beat: the careful girl finally speaks first.

chapters.title: Board Meeting, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. At the centennial board meeting, Quentin plays the recording publicly as Ferro live-publishes the archive. Whitlock tries to have her removed; students stand; Okafor arrives with a warrant. Emotional beat: climax — the room where silence lived learns noise.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Whitlock resigns mid-investigation and is indicted; Hargrove cooperates; the 1998 case is reopened. Quentin testifies, naming every number she ever counted. Emotional beat: justice outside the law finally entering it — imperfect, late, real.

chapters.title: Keys Returned
chapters.summary: Quentin and Marisol's dual POV. Reunited, Marisol returns the keyring; they visit the reopened natatorium memorial where Caleb's name is finally spoken aloud. Emotional beat: mourning that was forbidden for twenty-five years, allowed at last.

chapters.title: Semester's End
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, epilogue. Grades arrive unrigged for the first time; Quentin applies to colleges under her real name, loudly. She keeps one key on a chain — not as armor, but as memory. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; survival redefined as remembering out loud.
